name: Storm-Kiln Artist
oracle_text:
This creature gets +1/+0 for each artifact you control.
Magecraft — Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, create a Treasure token. (It's an artifact with "{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.")
blocked_sentences: Magecraft — Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, create a Treasure token. (It's an artifact with "{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.")

needs.what: A trigger that fires when an instant or sorcery spell is COPIED as well as when one is cast -- either a distinct `spell_copied` event raised wherever a copy of a spell is put on the stack (by `copy_spell`, `cast_copy`, storm, and replicate-style effects), or an opt-in flag on `spell_cast` (e.g. `include_copies: true`) that makes the existing event also fire for copies. It must fire once per copy, so a spell copied twice yields two triggers, and it must be controller-scoped ("whenever YOU cast or copy").
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `spell_cast` is the closest event in `trigger_events`, but a copy of a spell put onto the stack is not cast (CR 707.10a / 608.2), so `spell_cast` fires for the cast half only. Nothing else in `trigger_events` observes the stack -- the list has no copy-related event at all -- and the `copy_spell` / `cast_copy` ops are effects that a card performs, not events another permanent can watch. `condition_keys` offers only `was_cast`, which narrows a trigger to things that were cast rather than widening one to include copies, so it cannot recover the missing half. Shipping a bare `spell_cast` trigger would silently drop the printed "or copy" clause, which is exactly the approximation the brief forbids.

notes: The other printed line, "This creature gets +1/+0 for each artifact you control", IS expressible today: a static `buff` whose `power` is {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"]}} -- `count` is in `static_value_keys` and both `controller` and `types` are in `static_filter_keys`, and card type is a printed characteristic, so the load-time printed-characteristics rule is satisfied. The Treasure token itself is also not a blocker: `treasure_token` already exists in the engine's token pool (referenced from src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_cards.py). The card is blocked solely on the copy half of magecraft, so once that trigger lands the whole card is one `buff` static plus one triggered `create_token`.
